summary.headline: MSTC posted its highest-ever Q2 and H1 numbers, with H1 revenue from operations up over 25% YoY and PAT/PBT up about 42%, per management; no hard figures were given on the call.
summary.overview: Management described Q2 FY27 and H1 FY27 as record periods for the company, citing growth in revenue, PBT and PAT, and a return to positive profit at the joint venture after several loss-making years. Growth was attributed to higher scrap prices, a significant rise in iron ore volumes (more than 10-15%), and e-auction activity in mineral blocks and small land-parcel sales. The company received RBI in-principle approval for its TREDS platform, subject to conditions, and is awaiting final authorisation. Approvals for the EPR exchange and a proposed coal/mineral exchange remain pending, with no firm timeline given.

financial_highlights.value: Up more than 25% YoY (as stated by management)

financial_highlights.metric: PBT and PAT (H1 FY27, comparable period)
Cash and cash equivalents (30 Sep 2026 vs March)
financial_highlights.value: Up about 70% vs March, attributed to temporary timing of payments
About 20-25% of overall revenue (coal is part of this)

segments.name: E-auction / e-commerce platform
segments.commentary: Management cited growth in e-sale volumes in Q2 and H1, including mineral blocks and small land-parcel sales; no segment revenue figure was given.

segments.name: Mineral (incl. coal)
segments.commentary: Coal is reported within the mineral segment and cannot be separated; minerals comprise about 20-25% of revenue, with coal volume of about 1.54 million tonnes and roughly Rs 175 crore cited for the quarter, with no revenue split.

segments.name: Joint venture (scrap / metal JV)
segments.commentary: The JV turned positive after several loss-making years, with positive results for the last two to three quarters; management said it was near break-even earlier.

segments.name: TREDS platform
segments.commentary: RBI in-principle approval received two days before the call, subject to conditions; operations to start after final authorisation, with stabilisation expected over the next few months. Revenue model is a percentage of transaction fees.

segments.name: B2B travel portal
segments.commentary: Three players are active in the PSU B2B segment; management sees room for one more. B2C portal expected in three to six months.

guidance_outlook: Management is aiming for double-digit growth, and said the company has delivered 10-20% over the last three years; no range was given for the next two years.
TREDS revenue cannot be estimated until after the first quarter of operations, and it faces competition from four or five other TREDS platforms.
EPR exchange: management hopes for approval within this fiscal year but gave no timeline; approval is still awaited from CPCB and the ministry, and the company said six to eight months.
Coal/mineral exchange: management expects to decide within two to four months on whether to set it up, with a three-to-five-year window before exchange trading is fully operational.
Margins are expected to fluctuate and average out over four to six quarters, per management.
capex_capacity: No capex, capacity or utilisation figures were discussed on the call.
B2C travel portal to go live in three to six months.
Coal exchange: rules and operational setup expected to take three to five years.
demand_pricing: Scrap prices have hardened over the last two quarters, rising about 8-10% per quarter; management said it could not predict scrap prices, with logistics costs easing as more countries use domestic scrap.
Iron ore volumes rose more than 10-15% YoY; the company sold 1.54 million tonnes of iron ore and 4 lakh tonnes of bromide through its platform in the quarter.
Competitive bidding accounts for 30-40% or more of e-auction business, per management, with the rest being allocation to government and PSU clients.
Coal exchange: MSTC cites its domain expertise as an advantage against NSEC, which has received SEBI approval for the national coal exchange.

Government clients in the quarter: liquor licence auctions for a state government yielding about Rs 25 crore; land parcel auctions realising Rs 2,850 crore for Karnataka (as stated, possibly Rs 2,850 crore) on behalf of state entities.

qa_highlights.question: What is causing the delay in the EPR exchange and will it launch in phases?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the delay involves both regulatory approval and stakeholder interpretation, with five categories notified and more expected; no volume or value targets were given, and the timeline was given as six to eight months.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the proposed coal exchange and how does MSTC compare with NSEC?
qa_highlights.answer: The company is still assessing total market volume and its share; a decision is expected in two to four months. MSTC argued its legacy domain expertise is an advantage, and it expects the existing spot and linkage volumes to move to the exchange over three to five years.

qa_highlights.question: How much revenue did coal auctions contribute in the quarter (Rs 175 crore volume)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said coal revenue is commingled with the mineral segment and cannot be split out; mineral overall is about 20-25% of revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Why did cash rise about 70% from March?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said this reflects temporary timing of payments due on 30 September, and cash normally stays at about Rs 900-1,000 crore, so it has already normalised.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company enter data centres and what is the JV EBITDA run rate?
qa_highlights.answer: MSTC said it is not a data-centre business and has not evaluated one; it holds its own data centre for auction data. The JV has been positive for the last couple of quarters, but no EBITDA figure was given.

qa_highlights.question: Is the B2B travel business competitive and how large could it be?
qa_highlights.answer: Three players are active in the PSU B2B segment, with space for one more. Management declined to size the opportunity, and said the B2C portal will take three to six months.

risks_watch: EPR exchange approval is still pending with CPCB and the ministry, and no firm timeline has been given.
A coal/mineral exchange could move spot and linkage volumes away from MSTC, which would hit the mineral segment (about 20-25% of revenue).
TREDS market is crowded with four or five platforms, so transaction-fee revenue is uncertain until operations start.
Scrap price volatility; management called it unpredictable and cyclical, and the JV depends on scrap prices holding at current levels.
Margins are expected to fluctuate quarter to quarter, and the mix of revenue is lumpy (episodic auctions, not recurring).
summary.management_tone: Confident on the reported growth and the TREDS approval, but noticeably cautious and at times vague on the EPR and coal exchange timelines, and on segment-level numbers, which management declined to split out. Answers on revenue granularity and the coal business were often evasive, and the call had audio problems.

tone.note: Management was confident on reported growth and the TREDS approval but cautious and vague on EPR and coal exchange timelines and declined to split segment revenue; analysts pushed on coal revenue granularity, cash build-up, data-centre plans and the B2B travel market size.
